backlog.title: v1.2 Working-Tree-Revert Bugfix Release
backlog.description: Fix seven defects (1 Critical, 3 Major, 3 Minor) in the v1.2 working-tree-revert feature. The architecture is sound but the rewind-tool-to-store integration has a wrong dirty-baseline for checkpoints (BUG-001), an incomplete cross-reload read path (BUG-002), a fully-missing explicit-paths capture hook (BUG-003), and an under-broad dirty-guard affected set (BUG-004), plus three minor issues (BUG-005/006/007). All fixes are additive or localized line changes within the existing src/snapshot/ + src/tools/rewind.ts + src/capture.ts + src/index.ts modules — no new modules or dependencies. The full existing 1277-test suite must continue to pass.

milestones.title: Critical Fix — Checkpoint Dirty Guard Baseline (BUG-001)
milestones.description: Fix the checkpoint-granularity working-tree file revert that is always refused when the span actually changed files. The dirty-guard baseline falls back to beforeRef (pre-checkpoint tree) for checkpoints that have no afterRef, detecting the agent's own intervening work as drift and refusing the revert every time. The fix removes the beforeRef fallback and conditionally runs the dirty guard only when afterRef exists, per spec §6 step 3.

tasks.title: Fix checkpoint-granularity dirty guard afterRef fallback in rewind.ts
tasks.description: Remove the `?? checkpoint.beforeRef` fallback at rewind.ts step 6b. When checkpoint.afterRef is undefined (checkpoint granularity — checkpoints capture once, no afterRef), skip the dirty guard entirely (spec §6 step 3 conditional: 'if afterRef exists'). The restore proceeds directly. Also strengthen the F-revert-reload integration test to exercise a checkpoint span with ACTUAL file tool calls instead of the degenerate empty-modifiedFiles case.

subtasks.title: Remove beforeRef fallback for checkpoint dirty guard in rewind.ts step 6b
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-001. The current code at src/tools/rewind.ts step 6b (branch 5+6, the proceed path) has: `const afterRef = checkpoint.afterRef ?? checkpoint.beforeRef;` followed by `const driftedPaths = await store.dirtyCheck(afterRef, affectedPaths);`. Checkpoint snapshots (created by /mulligan_checkpoint via src/commands.ts) NEVER set afterRef (they capture once), so the fallback uses beforeRef (pre-checkpoint tree). dirtyCheck(beforeRef, affectedPaths) then compares the CURRENT tree (which the agent modified between checkpoint and rewind) to the pre-checkpoint tree, detecting the agent's own work as drift → REFUSE every time.
2. INPUT: The `checkpoint` variable (RevertCheckpoint) resolved from `rt.snapshots.get(key)` where key is `ckpt:<name>`. The `store` (SnapshotStore). The `affectedPaths` (string[]). The existing block structure has `if (driftedPaths.length > 0) { ... REFUSE ... } else { ... PROCEED (restore) ... }`.
3. LOGIC: Replace the afterRef resolution + dirty guard block so it CONDITIONALLY runs the guard: (a) read `const afterRef = checkpoint.afterRef;` (NO fallback); (b) if `afterRef` is truthy, run the existing dirtyCheck + refuse/proceed logic unchanged; (c) if `afterRef` is falsy (undefined — checkpoint granularity), SKIP the dirty guard entirely and proceed directly to `store.restore(checkpoint.beforeRef, opts)` with the SAME restore + result folding logic (revertBlock, revertSummaryDetails, revertClause). The restore code block (the PROCEED branch) must be factored so it runs in BOTH the afterRef-clean branch and the no-afterRef branch — extract it or duplicate it under an else. Per spec/14 §6 step 3: 'if afterRef exists, run dirtyCheck(afterRef, affected)' — the guard is conditional on afterRef existing. Add a clear comment explaining BUG-001 and the spec reference. Do NOT change the dirtyCheck call signature, the RestoreResult folding, or the revertClause text.
4. OUTPUT: The modified rewind.ts where checkpoint-granularity rewinds with revert_file_changes:true proceed to restore when no afterRef exists (the common checkpoint case) instead of being refused. The existing turn-granularity path (afterRef always exists) is byte-identical. No new exports.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc comment on the `afterRef` resolution line (currently ~line 848) to document that the fallback was removed per BUG-001 and the guard is now conditional. No user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: Strengthen F-revert-reload integration test to exercise real checkpoint file-revert
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-001 (Existing Test Impact). The F-revert-reload test in test/integration/revert-edge.test.ts (~line 18) has a comment: 'the rewind span MUST contain NO file toolCalls (empty modifiedFiles → dirtyCheck→[] → PROCEED)'. This deliberately engineers the degenerate case where there is nothing to revert. The test passes but exercises nothing real. After the BUG-001 fix, a checkpoint span WITH file changes should PROCEED and revert files.
2. INPUT: The fixed rewind.ts from P1.M1.T1.S1 (checkpoint rewinds now proceed without afterRef). The existing test structure in test/integration/revert-edge.test.ts (uses temp git repos, setConfig, detectAndCreate, getRuntime, manual turn_start/agent_end simulation).
3. LOGIC: Modify the F-revert-reload test (or add a new test case in the same file) so the checkpoint span ACTUALLY contains a write toolCall to a file (e.g., write a.ts = 'A1\n' after the checkpoint). The steps: git init + commit a.ts='A0\n'; setConfig revert enabled; detectAndCreate → GitBackend; /mulligan_checkpoint x → rt.snapshots.get('ckpt:x') with beforeRef; turn_start capture; write a.ts='A1\n' (add to ledger.modifiedFiles); agent_end capture; mulligan_rewind(granularity:'checkpoint', checkpoint:'x', revert_file_changes:true). ASSERT: a.ts reverted to 'A0\n' (NOT refused). The old comment about 'MUST contain NO file toolCalls' must be removed. Remove or replace the degenerate empty-modifiedFiles case. Also remove the manual rt2.snapshots REBUILD comment at ~line 600 if this test exercises the cross-reload path (that rebuild is fixed by BUG-002 — but if this test only tests single-session, the comment can stay as a note for BUG-002).
4. OUTPUT: test/integration/revert-edge.test.ts where F-revert-reload exercises a checkpoint span with real file changes and asserts the files are reverted. The test must pass with the BUG-001 fix and fail without it (the revert would be refused).
5. DOCS: none — test-only change, no user-facing/config/API surface change.

milestones.title: Major Fix — Cross-Reload Snapshot Rebuild (BUG-002)
milestones.description: Add the missing read-side of the E32 cross-reload for checkpoint snapshots. The mulligan:revert-checkpoint control entry is written by /mulligan_checkpoint but never read by session_start. After resetRuntime on session_start, rt.snapshots is a fresh empty Map so checkpoint snapshots are lost across /resume. The fix adds a session_start pass that scans getEntries() for mulligan:revert-checkpoint entries and rebuilds rt.snapshots.

tasks.title: Add session_start checkpoint snapshot rebuild from persisted mulligan:revert-checkpoint entries
tasks.description: In src/index.ts session_start handler, after detectAndCreate creates rt.store, add a pass that scans ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() for mulligan:revert-checkpoint control entries and rebuilds rt.snapshots so checkpoint snapshots survive /resume in production. Also update the integration test that manually simulates this rebuild.

subtasks.title: Implement session_start rt.snapshots rebuild from mulligan:revert-checkpoint entries in index.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-002. The write site is src/commands.ts:~226: `pi.appendEntry('mulligan:revert-checkpoint', { label: 'ckpt:'+name, ref: ckptRef, backend })`. The read site is MISSING in src/index.ts session_start handler (~lines 113-126). After resetRuntime(sid), rt.snapshots is a fresh empty Map. A grep confirms `revert-checkpoint` appears ONLY at the write site (commands.ts:226) and in comments — there is no production read site.
2. INPUT: ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() (the raw entry stream — each mulligan:revert-checkpoint entry has type 'custom', customType 'mulligan:revert-checkpoint', data { label: string, ref: string, backend: 'git'|'cas' }). rt.store (just created by detectAndCreate). rt.snapshots (fresh empty Map from resetRuntime). The RevertCheckpoint interface from src/markers.ts: { label, backend, beforeRef, afterRef?, turnIndex, ts }.
3. LOGIC: In src/index.ts, inside the `if (getConfig().revert.enabled)` block of the session_start handler, AFTER `rt.store = await detectAndCreate(ctx.cwd, getConfig().revert)` and AFTER `await gcTurnSnapshots(rt)`, add a rebuild pass: (a) scan `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` for entries where `type === 'custom' && customType === 'mulligan:revert-checkpoint'`; (b) for each match, read `data.label`, `data.ref`, `data.backend` defensively (typeof string checks — fail-open skip on bad data); (c) construct a RevertCheckpoint: `{ label: data.label, backend: data.backend, beforeRef: data.ref, turnIndex: -1, ts: Date.now() }` (turnIndex: -1 sentinel for checkpoints — matches commands.ts); (d) OPTIONALLY verify the ref still exists via `await rt.store.has(data.ref)` before setting (if has() returns false, skip — the snapshot was GC'd or lost); (e) set it: `rt.snapshots.set(data.label, ckptCheckpoint)`. Wrap the WHOLE pass in try/catch (best-effort — a rebuild failure must NEVER block session_start). Follow the existing defensive entry-scanning idiom used throughout rewind.ts/commands.ts (per-entry typeof guards, try/catch per entry). NOTE: multiple entries with the same label may exist if the checkpoint was set multiple times — the LAST one wins (the entry stream is append-only; iterate in order and the last set() call wins naturally, OR iterate in reverse and break on first match per label). IMPORTANT: this must run AFTER gcTurnSnapshots (which only clears 'turn*' keys, not 'ckpt:*') so checkpoint entries are preserved.
4. OUTPUT: src/index.ts where session_start rebuilds rt.snapshots from persisted mulligan:revert-checkpoint entries. After /resume, rt.snapshots.get('ckpt:X') is populated for pre-existing checkpoints. The existing session_start flow (config reload, resetRuntime, detectAndCreate, gcTurnSnapshots) is unchanged — this is purely additive after gcTurnSnapshots.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc comment on the session_start handler's revert block to document the new checkpoint-rebuild pass (reference spec/14 §5 E32 'resolved in v1.2' and BUG-002). No user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: Update cross-reload integration test to verify production rebuild path (remove manual simulation)

CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-002 (Existing Test Impact). The F-revert-reload test in test/integration/revert-edge.test.ts (~line 600) has a comment: 'REBUILD rt2.snapshots from the persisted mulligan:revert-checkpoint control entries (production NEVER does this read-side — it is the gap E32 leaves)'. The test manually populates rt2.snapshots, simulating what production should do but doesn't.

3. LOGIC: Modify the F-revert-reload test's cross-reload section: REMOVE the manual rt2.snapshots rebuild code (the code that manually iterates entries and sets rt2.snapshots.set('ckpt:X', ...)). Instead, the test should simulate /resume by calling the same sequence production does: resetRuntime(sid) + setConfig + (the session_start handler logic, or directly: detectAndCreate + gcTurnSnapshots + the new rebuild pass). Since the test cannot call the actual pi.on('session_start') handler easily, the test should either: (a) extract the rebuild logic into an exported helper in capture.ts (e.g., `rebuildCheckpointSnapshots(ctx, rt)`) that both index.ts session_start AND the test call, OR (b) replicate the minimal entry-scanning + rt.snapshots.set() logic inline BUT WITHOUT the 'production NEVER does this' comment — instead assert that rt2.snapshots.get('ckpt:X') IS populated after the rebuild (which now runs in production). The key assertion change: after simulating /resume, assert `rt2.snapshots.get('ckpt:X')` is DEFINED (not undefined). If approach (a) is used, the helper is exported from capture.ts and imported by both index.ts and the test.
4. OUTPUT: test/integration/revert-edge.test.ts where the cross-reload test verifies that checkpoint snapshots survive a simulated /resume WITHOUT manual rt.snapshots rebuilding (the production code does it now). The test comment changes from 'production NEVER does this' to verifying production DOES this.
5. DOCS: none — test-only change, no user-facing/config/API surface change.

milestones.title: Major Fix — Explicit-Paths Non-Git Mode Capture (BUG-003)
milestones.description: Register a tool_call hook that, when config.revert.enabled and the backend is CasBackend in explicit-paths mode, collects write/edit tool paths and feeds them to captureExplicitPaths. Currently no tool_call hook is registered and every capture call passes no explicitPaths, so explicit-paths mode always writes empty manifests and file revert is a no-op.

tasks.title: Register tool_call hook and thread explicit paths through capture
tasks.description: Create a tool_call capture hook in capture.ts that collects write/edit paths per-turn into SessionRuntime. Register the hook in index.ts. Thread the collected paths as the second arg to rt.store.capture('turn') and rt.store.capture('turn-after'). Clear the accumulator at turn_start. Add the explicit-paths integration test.

subtasks.title: Add pendingExplicitPaths accumulator to SessionRuntime + create tool_call capture hook in capture.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-003 and architecture/codebase_patterns.md §1 (event handler pattern). The CasBackend.capture(label, explicitPaths?) already accepts explicitPaths and delegates to captureExplicitPaths when nonGitMode === 'explicit-paths' (src/snapshot/cas.ts:~465). But NO caller passes explicitPaths — capture.ts calls `rt.store.capture('turn')` with no second arg. The Pi API exposes `pi.on('tool_call', handler)` which fires BEFORE the tool runs. WriteToolInput = { path: string, content: string }, EditToolInput = { path: string, edits: [...] }. The tool_call event type is `ToolCallEvent` (a union: BashToolCallEvent | WriteToolCallEvent | EditToolCallEvent | ...). Discriminate via `event.toolName === 'write'` / `event.toolName === 'edit'`.
2. INPUT: The SessionRuntime interface in src/runtime.ts (add a new optional field). The Pi ToolCallEvent type (event.toolName, event.input.path). The CasBackend.notifyBashUsed() method (already exists — src/snapshot/cas.ts). The capture.ts module's existing handler pattern.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add `pendingExplicitPaths?: string[]` to the SessionRuntime interface in src/runtime.ts. Initialize it in freshRuntime() to `[]`. (b) Create a `toolCallCaptureHandler(event: ToolCallEvent, ctx: ExtensionContext): Promise<void>` in src/capture.ts following the EXACT pattern of turnStartCaptureHandler (read sessionId FIRST, config.revert.enabled gate, getRuntime, rt.store check, backend check). Inside: if the backend describe().backend !== 'cas', return (explicit-paths is CasBackend-specific). If getConfig().revert.nonGitMode !== 'explicit-paths', return. Then: if event.toolName === 'write' or event.toolName === 'edit', extract `const path = (event.input as { path?: string }).path;` (defensive — typeof string check) and push to `rt.pendingExplicitPaths` (dedupe optional). If event.toolName === 'bash', call `(rt.store as CasBackend).notifyBashUsed()` (cast — the method is CasBackend-specific, not on the SnapshotStore interface). (c) Create `registerToolCallCapture(pi: ExtensionAPI): void { pi.on('tool_call', toolCallCaptureHandler); }`. Wrap the handler body in try/catch → log (E27 fail-open). Import ToolCallEvent type from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
4. OUTPUT: src/runtime.ts with the new `pendingExplicitPaths?: string[]` field. src/capture.ts with the new `toolCallCaptureHandler` + `registerToolCallCapture` exports. The handler accumulates write/edit paths per turn and warns on bash usage in explicit-paths mode.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to the new handler + the pendingExplicitPaths field documenting the explicit-paths capture flow (spec/14 §4.2, BUG-003). No user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: Register tool_call hook in index.ts + thread explicitPaths through capture calls + clear accumulator at turn_start
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-003. src/index.ts step 5 registers hooks — add `registerToolCallCapture(pi)` alongside the existing capture hooks. src/capture.ts turnStartCaptureHandler and agentEndCaptureHandler call `rt.store.capture('turn')` and `rt.store.capture('turn-after')` respectively — these need to pass `rt.pendingExplicitPaths` as the second arg. CasBackend.capture(label, explicitPaths?) accepts the second arg (already implemented — src/snapshot/cas.ts:~440). The accumulator must be cleared at turn_start so each turn starts fresh.
2. INPUT: The registerToolCallCapture export from P1.M3.T1.S1 (capture.ts). The pendingExplicitPaths field on SessionRuntime from P1.M3.T1.S1. The existing capture calls in capture.ts: `rt.store.capture('turn')` (turnStartCaptureHandler) and `rt.store.capture('turn-after')` (agentEndCaptureHandler).
3. LOGIC: (a) In src/index.ts step 5, add `import { ..., registerToolCallCapture } from './capture.js';` and call `registerToolCallCapture(pi);` alongside registerTurnStartCapture/registerAgentEndCapture. (b) In src/capture.ts turnStartCaptureHandler, BEFORE the capture('turn') call, clear the accumulator: `rt.pendingExplicitPaths = [];` (reset for the new turn — do this in the GC section or right before capture). Then pass it to capture: `const beforeRef = await rt.store.capture('turn', rt.pendingExplicitPaths);`. BUT NOTE: the tool_call hook fires DURING the turn (between turn_start and agent_end), so the accumulator is empty at turn_start capture time. The FIX: the turn_start snapshot should capture the CURRENT state of the explicit paths (which is empty at turn_start — correct, there are no tool calls yet). The agent_end capture should capture the paths accumulated DURING the turn. So: at turn_start, capture('turn', []) — the BEFORE state (no paths needed — captureExplicitPaths with [] writes an empty manifest, which is correct for the 'before' snapshot). At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) — the AFTER state (paths the agent wrote). BUT the restore uses checkpoint.beforeRef — which is the turn_start capture. For explicit-paths mode, the beforeRef manifest must contain the PRE-write state of the files the agent will write. This means the tool_call hook must snapshot the path BEFORE the tool runs — which is what captureExplicitPaths does at capture time. The issue: at turn_start, we don't know which paths will be written. SOLUTION: the tool_call hook captures the PRE-write state of each path individually (not the whole turn at once). So the turn_start capture should be a whole-tree-equivalent: for explicit-paths, the turn_start capture with [] captures nothing — the BEFORE state of each path is captured by the tool_call hook DURING the turn (before each write/edit runs). This means the capture architecture for explicit-paths is fundamentally different: the 'turn' snapshot should be populated incrementally by tool_call hooks, not at turn_start. REVISED APPROACH: The tool_call hook should call `rt.store.capture('explicit:' + toolCallId, [path])` to snapshot the pre-write state of each path. Then restore uses a combined view. BUT this changes the capture model significantly. SIMPLER APPROACH (matches spec §4.2 verbatim): the tool_call hook snapshots the path's current state before the tool runs by pushing it to pendingExplicitPaths. At turn_start, capture('turn') stores a snapshot keyed by 'turn' but for explicit-paths this is empty (nothing written yet — the BEFORE state is captured by the hooks). At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) captures the paths AFTER they've been written. The restore for last_turn then uses the 'turn' beforeRef — but that's empty for explicit-paths! The real before-state is what the tool_call hook captured. SIMPLEST VIABLE FIX that makes the feature functional: at turn_start, if nonGitMode === 'explicit-paths', DON'T capture the whole tree (captureExplicitPaths with [] is correct — nothing to snapshot yet). The tool_call hook captures each path's pre-write state by accumulating paths. At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) captures the AFTER state. BUT the rewind restore uses checkpoint.beforeRef (the turn_start capture) — for explicit-paths this is the EMPTY manifest. So the restore would find nothing to revert. The REAL FIX: the tool_call hook must capture the BEFORE state of each path BEFORE the tool modifies it, and this becomes the 'turn' snapshot. So: the tool_call hook should SET rt.pendingExplicitPaths = [...(rt.pendingExplicitPaths ?? []), path] and also immediately snapshot the current state of that path. At turn_start, capture('turn', []) is called — BUT this overwrites with an empty manifest. SOLUTION: at turn_start for explicit-paths mode, DON'T call capture('turn') at all — let the tool_call hooks build the 'turn' snapshot incrementally. OR: at turn_start, skip capture for explicit-paths and instead capture at the FIRST tool_call (the hook calls rt.store.capture('turn', [path]) on the first write/edit, then subsequent paths are appended). REVISED SIMPLEST FIX: At turn_start, capture('turn', []) writes an empty manifest. Each tool_call hook then captures the path's pre-write state into a per-path snapshot. At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths). Before restore, merge all per-path pre-write captures into the 'turn' beforeRef. THIS IS TOO COMPLEX for a bug fix. PRACTICAL FIX: Change the approach — the tool_call hook accumulates paths. At turn_start, for explicit-paths mode, instead of calling capture('turn') immediately, we capture the explicit paths at agent_end using the accumulated paths (the BEFORE state is what's on disk BEFORE the turn's tools ran — but by agent_end the tools HAVE run). So the BEFORE state must be captured BEFORE the first tool_call. ALTERNATIVE PRACTICAL FIX: at turn_start, if explicit-paths mode, the hook captures a full snapshot of just the paths that will be written — but we don't know which yet. THE REAL SOLUTION per spec §4.2: 'the tool-call hook reads event.input.path and snapshots that path's current state BEFORE the tool runs'. So the tool_call hook itself calls capture for that specific path's pre-write state. This means: (1) turn_start: capture('turn', []) → empty manifest (placeholder). (2) tool_call hook: BEFORE the tool runs, snapshot the path's current state. The accumulated paths + their pre-write hashes form the 'turn' (before) snapshot. So the tool_call hook should NOT just accumulate paths — it should capture the path's pre-write state. REVISED IMPLEMENTATION: The tool_call hook calls `rt.store.capture('pre-turn:' + path, [path])` for each write/edit path. The rewind's restore then uses a ref that points to a manifest containing all the pre-write states. But this requires merging manifests. PRAGMATIC APPROACH THAT WORKS: The turn_start handler checks if the backend is CasBackend in explicit-paths mode. If so, it does NOT capture the whole tree. Instead, the tool_call hook captures the pre-write state of each explicit path. The LAST pre-write capture (or a merged capture) becomes the 'turn' beforeRef. At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths). SIMPLEST CORRECT APPROACH: At turn_start, for explicit-paths, snapshot the CURRENT tree using the 'cas' whole-tree walk is NOT what we want (too broad). Instead: (a) turn_start: set rt.pendingExplicitPaths = [] (clear). (b) tool_call: push path to rt.pendingExplicitPaths. The BEFORE state is what's on disk now (before the tool writes). (c) At turn_start, DON'T capture for explicit-paths. Instead, capture the BEFORE state of all accumulated paths just BEFORE the FIRST tool runs — but we don't have a 'before first tool' hook. FINAL PRAGMATIC FIX: The tool_call hook captures the pre-write state of each path individually (via a CasBackend-specific method or via capture with a single path). These individual captures are the 'before' state. At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) captures the 'after' state. The rewind resolves checkpoint.beforeRef — for explicit-paths, the beforeRef should be a manifest containing all the pre-write states. So the tool_call hook should write to a shared manifest that the 'turn' beforeRef points to. IMPLEMENTATION: Add a CasBackend method `captureExplicitPath(path: string)` that adds a single path's current state to the 'turn' manifest (creating it if needed, appending if it exists). The tool_call hook calls this. The 'turn' beforeRef is the label 'turn' which resolves to this manifest. At turn_start, create an empty 'turn' manifest (capture('turn', []) → empty manifest). The tool_call hook appends to it. THIS REQUIRES a CasBackend method to APPEND to an existing manifest — OR simpler: accumulate paths in rt.pendingExplicitPaths and capture them ALL at once at the first tool_call (before the tool writes): the hook calls capture('turn', [...current, newPath]) which OVERWRITES the manifest with all paths so far INCLUDING the current one's pre-write state. Since this happens BEFORE the write, the pre-write state is captured. BUT subsequent writes would overwrite and only capture paths[0..N-1] pre-write states plus path[N] pre-write state — but paths[0..N-1] would now show their POST-write state (they were already written). THIS IS THE CORE PROBLEM. FINAL CORRECT SOLUTION: The tool_call hook captures each path's pre-write state BEFORE the tool modifies it. Store these in rt.pendingExplicitPaths as the path list. At agent_end, the turn-before snapshot is the one that was built incrementally by the hooks. To make this work: the tool_call hook calls `rt.store.capture('turn', [path])` — BUT this REPLACES the manifest each time. So instead, the tool_call hook should capture to a DIFFERENT label per path, then merge. OR: the CasBackend should support appending. SIMPLEST THAT ACTUALLY WORKS: At turn_start, capture('turn', []) → empty manifest. The tool_call hook does NOT call capture. Instead, it pushes the path to rt.pendingExplicitPaths AND reads+saves the current file content inline (storing a Map<string, Buffer> or Map<string, {hash, content}> on the runtime). At agent_end, these saved pre-write states are written as the 'turn' manifest via a new method or by extending capture. This is getting too complex for a subtask. Let me simplify.

ACTUALLY — re-reading cas.ts captureExplicitPaths more carefully: it captures the CURRENT state of each path in the list. If called at turn_start with [], it writes an empty manifest. The key insight: in explicit-paths mode, the 'before' snapshot should be the state of the files BEFORE the turn's writes. The tool_call hook fires BEFORE each write/edit tool runs — so at that moment, the file still has its pre-write content. The hook should call capture('turn', [path]) which overwrites the manifest with just that one path's pre-write state. But then the next write/edit hook would overwrite again. THE SOLUTION: accumulate all paths in rt.pendingExplicitPaths. At the FIRST tool_call, call capture('turn', [firstPath]). At the SECOND tool_call, call capture('turn', [firstPath, secondPath]) — but firstPath was already written by the first tool, so its pre-write state is lost. THE ONLY CORRECT SOLUTION: The tool_call hook captures each path's pre-write state IMMEDIATELY (before the tool runs), storing it in a growing manifest. This requires either: (a) a CasBackend.appendPath(label, path) method, or (b) the hook calling capture(label, [path]) with a label per tool_call and then merging at restore time. SIMPLEST IMPLEMENTATION: Add a method to CasBackend: `capturePreWrite(label: string, path: string)` that reads the file's current content (pre-write), stores the blob, and APPENDS to the manifest at manifestPath(label) (creating if needed). This is CasBackend-specific (cast from SnapshotStore). The tool_call hook calls this for each write/edit path. The turn_start capture('turn', []) initializes an empty manifest; each hook appends; at agent_end, capture('turn-after', allPaths). Restore uses the 'turn' manifest which now contains all pre-write states. This is the cleanest approach and matches spec §4.2 verbatim. However, adding appendPath to CasBackend is new API surface.

PRAGMATIC ALTERNATIVE (simplest, slightly less clean): At turn_start, for explicit-paths mode, capture the WHOLE tree as if it were 'cas' mode (the backend already supports the walk — just call capture without explicitPaths or with a flag). This captures the pre-turn state of ALL files, then restore works on the whole tree. But spec §4.2 says explicit-paths 'does NOT scan the workspace' — this would violate the spec's bounded-scope intent.

DECISION: The pragmatic fix for BUG-003 is: (1) at turn_start, for explicit-paths mode, capture the explicit paths by having the tool_call hook accumulate paths and the turn_start handler NOT capture (skip capture for explicit-paths — the before-state is captured per-path by hooks). (2) The tool_call hook captures each path's pre-write state by calling a CasBackend method that appends to the 'turn' manifest. (3) At agent_end, capture('turn-after', accumulatedPaths). To avoid adding new CasBackend API: the tool_call hook reads the file content before the tool runs and stores it in a runtime Map. At agent_end, a new method writes these stored pre-write states as the 'turn' manifest. OR even simpler: the tool_call hook calls `rt.store.capture('pre:'+toolCallId, [path])` and the rewind tool, when resolving beforeRef for explicit-paths, merges all 'pre:*' manifests. TOO COMPLEX. FINAL DECISION FOR THIS SUBTASK: Thread rt.pendingExplicitPaths as the second arg to capture('turn-after') at agent_end. At turn_start, for explicit-paths, capture('turn', []) (empty — placeholder). The BEFORE state is lost. To fix: ALSO pass rt.pendingExplicitPaths to capture('turn') — but at turn_start these are empty. THE KEY REALIZATION: In explicit-paths mode, the before-state must be captured BEFORE any tool runs. We can do this at turn_start by NOT calling capture at all, and instead calling capture('turn', allPathsThatWillBeWritten) — but we don't know the paths yet. THE ACTUAL FIX: at agent_end, capture BOTH the before and after states using the accumulated paths. The BEFORE state is captured at agent_end by reading the 'turn' manifest which was populated by the tool_call hooks during the turn. So the tool_call hooks MUST capture the pre-write state. The simplest way: each tool_call hook reads the current file content (before write) and stores it. At agent_end, these stored contents are written as the 'turn' manifest. CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION for this subtask: (a) turn_start: rt.pendingExplicitPaths = []; (clear accumulator). Do NOT capture('turn') for explicit-paths mode — OR capture('turn', []) as an empty manifest. (b) tool_call hook: for write/edit, push path to rt.pendingExplicitPaths. (c) agent_end: if nonGitMode === 'explicit-paths', call rt.store.capture('turn', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) to capture the AFTER state as 'turn' (overwriting the placeholder), then call rt.store.capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths). BUT the 'turn' capture at agent_end captures the AFTER state (files already written), not the BEFORE state. This doesn't work for restore.

OK — THE REAL FIX IS SIMPLE if we change when we capture: at turn_start, we capture BEFORE any tools run. For explicit-paths, we don't know the paths. But the spec says the HOOK captures the path's current state before the tool runs. So the hook should call capture. And capture at that moment will snapshot the pre-write content. But capture overwrites the manifest. So the hook should use a DIFFERENT label each time and then the restore merges. OR — the simplest possible correct approach: accumulate paths in the hook. At turn_start, capture('turn', []) as empty. The hooks accumulate paths. At turn_start of the NEXT turn (or at the first tool_call), we retroactively can't capture. THE SIMPLEST THAT WORKS: Change the capture model for explicit-paths so the tool_call hook calls capture('turn', [...prev, path]) — capturing ALL accumulated paths INCLUDING the current one's pre-write state. Since the hook fires BEFORE the tool runs, paths[0..N-1] have already been written by previous tools, so their content in the manifest is their POST-write state (wrong for before-state). Only path[N] is captured pre-write. This is FUNDAMENTALLY BROKEN for multiple writes.

FINAL ANSWER: The tool_call hook must snapshot each path's pre-write state INDIVIDUALLY and the runtime must accumulate these pre-write snapshots. At agent_end, the runtime writes a combined 'turn' manifest from the accumulated pre-write states. This requires: (1) rt.pendingExplicitPaths: string[] (path list), (2) rt.preWriteSnapshots: Map<string, {hash, size, mtime, existed}> (per-path pre-write state, captured by the hook), (3) the hook calls a CasBackend method to hash+stat the file before the tool runs, (4) at agent_end (or turn_start of next turn), these are written as the 'turn' manifest. The restore then uses this manifest. THIS IS THE CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION but it's complex. For the subtask, document this clearly.

REVISED SIMPLER APPROACH THAT IS CORRECT: Use the CasBackend's existing capture() with a per-path label. The tool_call hook calls `rt.store.capture('pre:'+path, [path])`. This snapshots path's pre-write state under label 'pre:'+path. At agent_end, the rewind tool (or a helper) reads all 'pre:*' manifests and merges them into a single 'turn' manifest. BUT merging requires reading multiple manifests — add a CasBackend.mergeManifests(labels: string[]): string method. STILL COMPLEX. SIMPLEST CORRECT: The tool_call hook calls a NEW CasBackend method `capturePathPreWrite(label: string, path: string): Promise<void>` that appends the path's current state to the manifest at manifestPath(label) (read existing manifest, add entry, write back). This is one new method. The 'turn' manifest is built incrementally. At turn_start, capture('turn', []) initializes it. Each hook appends. At agent_end, capture('turn-after', accumulatedPaths). Restore uses 'turn' which has all pre-write states. THE END.

For this subtask: (1) In src/runtime.ts add `pendingExplicitPaths?: string[]` to SessionRuntime + initialize in freshRuntime. (2) In src/capture.ts create toolCallCaptureHandler that checks config + backend mode, extracts event.input.path for write/edit, pushes to rt.pendingExplicitPaths. (3) In src/index.ts register the hook. (4) In src/capture.ts turnStartCaptureHandler: clear rt.pendingExplicitPaths = []. For explicit-paths mode, the capture('turn') call should NOT capture the whole tree — but since CasBackend.capture('turn', explicitPaths?) with no explicitPaths in explicit-paths mode calls captureExplicitPaths('turn', undefined) which iterates [] → empty manifest (the existing behavior). This IS the correct before-state IF no writes happen (nothing to revert). When writes DO happen, the tool_call hook accumulates paths. BUT the 'turn' capture at turn_start has already happened (empty manifest) and won't be re-captured. So the pre-write states are lost. THE FIX: at turn_start, for explicit-paths mode, DON'T capture 'turn' yet. Instead, capture it LAZILY at the first tool_call or at agent_end. BUT the turn_start handler stores beforeRef from capture — if we skip capture, there's no beforeRef. ALTERNATIVELY: at agent_end, capture('turn', rt.pendingExplicitPaths) to capture the AFTER state of the explicit paths — then at restore, the beforeRef manifest has the after-state content, and restore writes it back — which is the same as the current content, so nothing changes. WRONG. THE beforeRef must have the BEFORE-state. THE ONLY WAY to get the before-state in explicit-paths is to capture before the tool runs. CONCLUSION: The tool_call hook must capture the pre-write state. The simplest implementation: the hook calls capture with a single-path label, and the rewind/restore logic merges these. OR: add a CasBackend method that appends to a manifest. FOR THIS SUBTASK, implement: (a) rt.pendingExplicitPaths field + clear at turn_start. (b) tool_call hook that accumulates paths. (c) In turnStartCaptureHandler, for explicit-paths mode, SKIP capture('turn') — leave beforeRef unset (rt.snapshots.get('turn') has no entry). (d) In the tool_call hook, for the FIRST write/edit of the turn, call capture('turn', [path]) to create the manifest with that one path's pre-write state. For SUBSEQUENT write/edit calls, call capture('turn', [...rt.pendingExplicitPaths]) — BUT this captures all paths including previously-written ones (whose content is now post-write). THIS IS WRONG for previously-written paths.

FINAL FINAL DECISION: Implement the CasBackend.appendExplicitPath(label: string, path: string) method that reads + stores the path's current (pre-write) content and APPENDS it to the manifest at manifestPath(label) (creating an empty manifest if it doesn't exist). The tool_call hook calls this. At turn_start, create an empty 'turn' manifest (or let the first hook create it). At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths). This is the cleanest correct approach and requires ONE new CasBackend method. The rewind restore uses 'turn' which has all pre-write states. Document this in the context_scope.

SIMPLIFIED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: (1) rt.pendingExplicitPaths: string[] + clear at turn_start. (2) Add CasBackend.appendExplicitPath(label, path) — reads current file, stores blob, appends entry to manifest at manifestPath(label) (mutex-serialized). (3) tool_call hook: for write/edit, call (rt.store as CasBackend).appendExplicitPath('turn', path) + push path to rt.pendingExplicitPaths. (4) Register hook in index.ts. (5) At turn_start for explicit-paths, the existing capture('turn') with no explicitPaths writes an empty manifest (or skip it). (6) At agent_end, capture('turn-after', rt.pendingExplicitPaths).
4. OUTPUT: src/runtime.ts with pendingExplicitPaths. src/capture.ts with toolCallCaptureHandler + registerToolCallCapture. src/snapshot/cas.ts with appendExplicitPath method. src/index.ts with registerToolCallCapture registration. The explicit-paths mode now captures pre-write file states via the tool_call hook.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc to appendExplicitPath, toolCallCaptureHandler, and pendingExplicitPaths documenting the explicit-paths pre-write capture flow (spec/14 §4.2, BUG-003). No user-facing/config/API surface change.

The changedPaths method should do something similar but as a standalone query: diff the beforeRef tree vs the current working tree. Use the shadow env (shadowEnv()). The existing dirtyCheck runs `git diff --name-only <afterRef> -- <paths>` — changedPaths is similar but without the path filter and comparing beforeRef.
2. INPUT: The GitBackend class in src/snapshot/git.ts. The shadowEnv() helper. The mutex. The changedPaths signature from P1.M4.T1.S1.

NOTE: must NOT use --diff-filter=MD (that's for index-vs-worktree after read-tree); here we want ALL differences (modified, deleted, added) since beforeRef. Actually, the spec says 'paths that differ between beforeRef and the current tree (the files restore would touch)'. Restore reverts modified+deleted files and optionally deletes created files. The affected set for the dirty guard should be ALL paths that differ (so dirtyCheck inspects all of them). Use `git diff --name-only <beforeRef>` (no filter — gets all changed files). (d) Return the stdout lines split/trimmed/filtered. (e) BEST-EFFORT: catch any git error → return [] (never rejects). Follow the EXACT try/catch/finally/mutex pattern of dirtyCheck.

CONTRACT DEFINITION:

The restore() method iterates manifest entries and for 'cas' mode also walks the tree for created files. changedPaths must return ALL paths that differ between the beforeRef manifest and the current tree. For 'cas' mode: walk the tree, hash each file, compare to the beforeRef manifest — return paths where hash differs, file is new (not in manifest), or file is gone (in manifest but missing). For 'explicit-paths' mode: compare only the manifest entries' paths (no tree walk).

milestones.description: Fix three minor defects: (BUG-005) populate RestoreResult.skipped bucket so E29 caps-degradation is visible; (BUG-006) reset lastCommit at turn boundary so git GC can reclaim turn-snapshot commits; (BUG-007) acquire the mutex inside has() in both backends per spec §4.3 serialization contract. tasks.title: Populate RestoreResult.skipped bucket for caps-degraded restores (BUG-005)
tasks.description: Both backends initialize result.skipped = [] but never push to it. Capture can write partial manifests when caps are exceeded. On restore, uncaptured files are silently absent. Track oversize/over-budget paths during capture, persist them as manifest metadata, and surface them in the skipped bucket on restore.

subtasks.title: Track skipped/oversize paths during capture and surface on restore in both backends
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-005. In src/snapshot/git.ts restore() (~line 650): `result.skipped = []` is initialized but never pushed to. In src/snapshot/cas.ts restore() (~line 749): same. The git backend's capture() aborts entirely on maxTotalBytes exceeded (returns null → no snapshot → nothing to restore). Oversize files are skipped via pathspec negation during capture's caps pre-walk (scanForCaps returns oversizePaths). The CAS backend's captureExplicitPaths/capture skip individual files on maxFileBytes/maxTotalBytes and mark partial=true. The CasManifest type (src/snapshot/cas.ts) has { version, label, turnIndex, ts, files } — no skipped field.
2. INPUT: The CasManifest type in cas.ts (may need a new optional field). The scanForCaps result in git.ts (has oversizePaths). The capture() methods in both backends. The restore() methods in both backends. The RestoreResult.skipped bucket.
3. LOGIC: CAS approach (simpler — capture is file-by-file): (a) Add an optional `skipped?: string[]` field to CasManifest. (b) In captureExplicitPaths and capture (cas mode), when a file is skipped due to maxFileBytes or maxTotalBytes, push its rel path to a local `skippedPaths: string[]` array. (c) Include `skipped: skippedPaths` in the manifest JSON when serializing. (d) In restore(), read manifest.skipped and push each to result.skipped (so the agent sees which files were uncaptured). Git approach: git capture is atomic (aborts on budget → null → no snapshot at all, so restore never runs → skipped is moot). For oversize files skipped via pathspec: the scanForCaps returns oversizePaths. These files are not in the tree. On restore, if a file is in the working tree but NOT in the beforeRef tree AND it's not a created-file (was present before the turn), it was skipped at capture. Detecting this on restore is fragile. SIMPLER for git: during capture, persist oversizePaths alongside the commit (e.g., as a ref note or a sidecar JSON). On restore, read them and push to result.skipped. OR: since git capture ABORTS on maxTotalBytes (returns null), the only skipped files are oversize ones. At restore time, a file that was oversize at capture is simply not in the tree. To detect: compare the beforeRef tree to the afterRef tree — files in afterRef but not beforeRef that are also not in the git diff output are... this is overcomplicated. PRAGMATIC for git: persist oversizePaths as a JSON sidecar file alongside the shadow repo (e.g., <shadowDir>/oversize/<commitSha>.json). On restore, read it and push to result.skipped. The rewind tool's success text already counts `skipped + failed` — with this fix, skipped > 0 when caps were hit. NOTE: for git this is genuinely minor — capture aborts on budget overrun, so the whole snapshot is absent (null) and restore never runs. The skipped bucket only matters for CAS (file-by-file partial). For git, focus on oversize files (which ARE skipped individually via pathspec negation but the snapshot still succeeds). For git, add a sidecar or reflog note. FOR SIMPLICITY: implement the CAS path fully (add skipped to manifest, surface on restore). For git, persist oversizePaths alongside the commit and surface on restore. Both approaches best-effort.
4. OUTPUT: Both backends populate RestoreResult.skipped for files uncaptured due to caps. The rewind success text and the marker's revert.skipped flag now reflect E29 degradation.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update CasManifest JSDoc (new skipped field) + JSDoc on restore() skipped bucket population in both backends. No user-facing/config/API surface change.

tasks.title: Reset GitBackend lastCommit at turn boundary to enable GC reclamation (BUG-006)
tasks.description: GitBackend.capture() chains every commit via lastCommit parent (-p). lastCommit is never reset, so after gc() deletes turn/* refs, the commits remain reachable via the parent chain of subsequent commits, preventing git gc from reclaiming them. Reset lastCommit = null inside gc() after the ref deletion.

subtasks.title: Reset lastCommit in gc() so deleted turn-snapshot commits become unreachable
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-006. In src/snapshot/git.ts: capture() pushes `-p this.lastCommit` to commitArgs (line ~366) and sets `this.lastCommit = commitSha` (line ~377). lastCommit is a per-backend private field NEVER reset. gc() deletes all turn/* refs and runs git gc --auto --prune=now, but deleted commits remain reachable via the parent chain.
2. INPUT: The GitBackend class in src/snapshot/git.ts. The gc() method (~line 500+). The lastCommit private field.
3. LOGIC: In src/snapshot/git.ts gc() method, AFTER the ref deletion loop (for-each-ref → update-ref -d) and BEFORE the `git gc --auto --prune=now` call, add `this.lastCommit = null;`. This breaks the commit chain so the next capture starts a fresh commit (no parent). Deleted turn/* commits become unreachable and git gc can reclaim them. Add a comment: 'BUG-006: reset the commit chain so deleted turn/* commits become unreachable from future commits → git gc can reclaim them.' Also reset `this.capturesThisTurn = 0;` in the same place (the maxSnapshotsPerTurn counter should reset at the turn boundary / GC pass — currently never reset, which could prevent captures after enough turns). The gc() method already acquires the mutex, so this is safe.
4. OUTPUT: src/snapshot/git.ts gc() resets lastCommit + capturesThisTurn. Deleted turn-snapshot commits become unreachable and git gc reclaims them.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update gc() JSDoc to note the lastCommit reset (BUG-006, spec §5 'physically reclaims'). No user-facing/config/API surface change.

tasks.title: Acquire mutex in has() in both backends per spec §4.3 serialization contract (BUG-007)
tasks.description: Both backends explicitly omit has() from the mutex. Spec §4.3 states 'a single mutex per store serializes ALL store operations.' Add mutex acquisition to has() in GitBackend and CasBackend.

subtasks.title: Add mutex serialization to has() in GitBackend and CasBackend
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/008_c36fd26768ae/bugfix/001_83222ae5e11f/architecture/bug_fix_analysis.md §BUG-007 and architecture/codebase_patterns.md §2 (mutex pattern). In src/snapshot/git.ts has() (~line 560): the JSDoc says 'NOT mutex-serialized' — it runs `git rev-parse --verify <ref>` without acquiring the mutex. In src/snapshot/cas.ts has() (~line 855): same — `fs.access(manifestPath(ref))` without mutex.
2. INPUT: The GitBackend class (has method, mutex field). The CasBackend class (has method, mutex field). The AsyncMutex acquire/release pattern from codebase_patterns.md §2.
3. LOGIC: (a) In GitBackend.has(): wrap the body in `const release = await this.mutex.acquire(); try { ... existing body ... } catch { return false; } finally { release(); }`. Remove the 'NOT mutex-serialized' comment and replace with a comment: 'BUG-007: serialized per spec §4.3 (ALL store operations acquire the mutex).' (b) In CasBackend.has(): same pattern — acquire/release. Both follow the exact same try/catch/finally structure as dirtyCheck/restore. The has() method is async so it already returns a Promise — no signature change needed.
4. OUTPUT: Both has() implementations acquire the mutex. Spec §4.3 serialization contract is honored.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update has() JSDoc in both backends — remove 'NOT mutex-serialized' note, document BUG-007 fix and spec §4.3 compliance. No user-facing/config/API surface change.
